newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt volatilities under pressure.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt volatilities under pressure.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options came under pressure as underlying markets rallied and traders took out risk premiums out of option prices after a bundle of benign economic data, dealers said.

They said volatilities had been inflated earlier in the week ahead of Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and October producer price index (PPI) as well as today's October consumer price index (CPI) and retail sales.
"Vols have been coming off since right after FOMC," said a brokerage trader at Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT). "It hasn't paid to be long options."
Implied volatility for CBOT January T-bond futures options was down a quarter point from late Wednesday levels at around 10.0 percent in the early afternoon.

The CBOT trader said today's economic data, as well as Wednesday's numbers and the FOMC meeting, at which the Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady, did little to damage the bond market's recent uptrend and have hurt those who had been anticipating a pull-back.
Early in the session, October CPI came in at up 0.3 percent overall and up 0.2 percent excluding food and energy, in line with economists' average forecasts.
October retail sales rose 0.2 percent overall and 0.4 percent excluding autos, also largely in line with expectations.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, front-month volatilities were hammered by prospects of a steady near-term U.S. monetary policy.
In Eurodollar options, there were a lot of calendar spreads involving selling of March volatilities, traders said.
Implied volatilities for March and June Eurodollar futures options were off 0.3 point each to about 10.7 and 15.1 percent respectively.
Still, caution about an overdue correction led to some bargain hunting.

"We're beginning to see some interested buyers at these levels," said an investment bank trader at Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "(They are) not aggressive, but just beginning to work bids and starting to buy a little bit."
